title: The record and the signs
summary: The record recounts the record keeper’s righteousness and miracles, the passing of the thirty-third year, and the people’s expectation of Samuel’s sign amid doubts and disputes.

explicit_facts.text: The record keeper was just and did many miracles in the name of Jesus; he could do so only if cleansed from iniquity.
The account says the thirty-third year had passed, with a qualification about possible reckoning error.
The people earnestly expected Samuel the Lamanite’s sign of three days of darkness.
Doubtings and disputations arose among the people despite the signs given.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A group of people may be shown in discussion or looking expectantly; the text does not specify an individual conversation.
unspecified_visual_details: The record keeper’s identity, appearance, and location are not stated.
The people’s appearance, exact number, and setting are not stated.

the people began to look with great earnestness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The three days of darkness are anticipated here; their onset occurs later.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a miracle or the three days of darkness as already occurring.

title: The storm begins

explicit_facts.text: A great storm arose on the fourth day of the first month of the thirty-fourth year.
